description_en: Lo Gekar might be contemporaneous with the first monastery of Tibet, Samyé, which was founded in the late 8thcentury. Its foundation is recorded in thePema Katang(pad+ma bka’ thang), a text containing the biography of Padmasambhava, the teacher credited with taming of local deities across the Himalayas. This text was discovered by the treasure revealer Orgyen Lingpa (o rgyan gling pa; b. 1323), his date thus providing aterminus ante quemfor the original temple. The relevant account is found in canto 62, recording the completion of Samyé Monastery. Lo Gekhar is clearly described as the monastery of White Virtue with the surrounding chörten and springs part of the holy site. This account also explains why Lo Gekhar is of great cultural and religious importance to the Mustang region and to Tibetan Buddhism at large. The temple is frequently visited by pilgrims from the region and beyond. The complex is also used by villagers from Marang and Tsarang for special rituals. (see Luczanits: Seismic Strengthening and Restoration of Lo Gekhar, project proposal, 2020).The temple of Lo Gekhar is located at an altitude of 3930 meters on the south bank of the Marang River, a tributary to the Kali Gandaki, in Upper Mustang. It sits at the head of the valley that houses the villages of Marang and Tsarang, the latter being one of the largest villages in the valley and a key settlement in the history of the historical Kingdom of Lo. The complex is owned and maintained by the village of Marang. Two approach roads have been constructed recently on either side of the valley, the one on the side of Marang village considerably easier to maintain. Both are linked to the main road passing by Tsarang.The monument as it stands today predominantly dates from the last decades of the 16thcentury onwards, a restoration of the complex being recorded at that time.Architecturally, the complex can be divided into two sections: the northern half, painted red, is the actual temple (lha khangorgtsug lag khang), and the southern part, the religious mansion (pho brang) is directly adjacent to it and forms an integral part of the temple. The temple has four distinct structural unitsL01: the Guru Lhakhang (gu ru lha khang), a two storied sanctum housing the main statues; L02: the assembly hall in front of it; L03: the Gönkhang (dgon khang) a protector’s chapel to the right of the assembly hall; L04: the roofed entry area.Of these, the core structure with its massive ten foot thick walls may well have once been the base of a tower as narrated in the Pema Katang. There is little information available regarding past restorations. As legend informs the originally nine-story tall temple collapsed in an earthquake and was never rebuilt to its original size.According to the caretaker the original entry to the assembly hall was from the south and accessed from the mansion’s courtyard (L09). Sometimes in the late 1970s a lama from Lo Manthang moved to Lo Gekar and built a two-story structure in the courtyard; the lower room (L10) was used as a stable and the room above for his residence (U10-today called the “VIP room”). It is not documented when the portico was added to the temple’s east facade and the new main entrance created. The caretaker also reports that this lama was responsible for rebuilding the chörtens at the corners of Lo Gekar.In 2003-2004 the northern half of the complex was restored under the guidance of John Sunday with funding from the American Himalayan Foundation.
description_ne: ईश्वीको ८ औं शताव्दीको अन्ततिर बनाइएको लो गेखर गुम्बालाई मुस्ताङको सबैभन्दा पुरानो बौद्ध सम्पदाका रूपमा लिइन्छ । यो गुम्बा तिब्बतमा ८ औं शताव्दीको अन्ततिर बनाइएको साम्ये गुम्बाको समकालिन हुनसक्छ ।  गुरु पद्मसम्भवको जीवनी समेटिएको 'पेमा कताङ्ग' नामक पुस्तकमा यस गुम्बाको निर्माणका बारेमा उल्लेख गरिएको छ । यो पुस्तक सन् १३२३ मा जन्मेका उर्गेन लिङ्गपाले भेट्टाएका थिए । यसबाट पनि यो गुम्बाको प्राचीनता देखाउछ । गुम्बासंग सम्बन्धित विवरण उक्त पुस्तकको श्लोक ६२ मा पाइन्छ जसमा साम्ये गुम्बाको निर्माण सम्पन्न भएको कुरा लेखिएको छ । लो गेखर गुम्बालाई 'Monastery of White Virtue' का रूपमा वर्णन गरिएको छ । यस वरपरका छोर्तेनहरूलाई पनि गुम्बाकै अंगका रूपमा लिइएको छ । मुस्ताङ क्षेत्र लगायत समग्र रूपमा तिब्बती बुद्धधर्मका लागि समेत लो गेखर गुम्बा धार्मिक र सांस्कृतिक रूपमा महत्वपूर्ण रहेको यी टिपोटहरूले दर्शाउछ । यस क्षेत्र लगायत बाहिरका पनि तीर्थयात्रीहरू नियमित रूपमा यो गुम्बा दर्शन गर्न आउँछन् । मराङ र सराङ गाउँका वासिन्दाले विभिन्न पुजाआजाका लागि पनि गुम्बालाई प्रयोग गर्छन् (हेर्नुहोस्: Luczanits: Seismic strengthening and Restoration of Lo Gekhar, project proposal, 2020) ।कालीगण्डकीको एक सहायक नदी मराङ खोलाको दक्षिणी किनारमा अवस्थित लो गेखर गुम्बा ३,९३० मीटर उँचाइमा रहेको छ । मराङ र सराङ गाउँहरू रहेको उपल्लो मुस्ताङ उपत्यकाको टुप्पोमा यो गुम्बा रहेको छ । यस क्षेत्रको सबैभन्दा ठूला गाउँहरू मध्ये एक सराङ गाउ ऐतिहासिक लो राज्यको इतिहासकै एक प्रमुख वस्ती हो । यस गुम्बा मराङ गाउले रेखदेख गर्दै आएको छ । उपत्यकाको दुबैतिरबाट गुम्बालाई जोड्ने दुई सडक हालै निर्माण गरिएको छ । दुबै सडक सराङ हुँदै जाने मूलसडकसंग जोडिएको छ । दुई मध्ये मराङ गाउँ हुँदै जाने सडकको अवस्था राम्रो छ ।अहिले रहेका गुम्बाका केही प्रमुख संरचनाहरू १६ औं शताव्दीका अन्तिम केही दशकहरूतिर बनेको देखिन्छ । त्यसबेला गुम्बाको जिर्णोद्धार गरिएको प्रमाण छ ।गुम्बाको भौतिक स्वरूपलाई दुई अंशमा बाँड्न सकिन्छ: रातो रंग लगाइएको उत्तरी अंश जहाँ मुख्य गुम्बा रहेको छ, र यसको संगै रहेको दक्षिणी अंश जहाँ धार्मिक भवन रहेको छ । मूल गुम्बा उत्तरी अंशमा रहे पनि दक्षिणी अंश पनि गुम्बाकै अभिन्न अंग हो । संरचनागत रूपमा भने गुम्बालाई चार अंशमा बाँड्न सकिन्छ:L01: गुरु ल्हाखाङ – गुम्बाको गर्भगृहका रूपमा रहेको यो दुईतल्ले संरचनामा मूलमूर्तिहरू स्थापना गरिएका छन्,L02: सभाकक्ष – यो गुरु ल्हाखाङको ठीक अगाडी रहेको छ,L03: गोङखाङ – सभाकक्षको दायाँतर्फ रहेको भवन, रL04: छाना सहितको प्रवेशमार्ग ।गुम्बाको मुख्य अंशका भित्ताहरू दश फीट बाक्ला छन् । कुनै समयमा यी संरचनाहरू पेमा कताङले व्याख्या गरेको ठूलो भवनकै एक अंश हुनुपर्छ । विगतमा यहाँ गरिएका जिर्णोद्धारका बारेमा निक्कै कम मात्र जानकारी पाइन्छ । तर एक भूकम्पमा नौ तल्ले गुम्बा भत्किएको र फेरि पुरानै स्वरूपमा कहिल्यै नबनाइएको किम्वदन्ती भने रहेको छ ।सभाकक्ष प्रवेश गर्ने मूलढोका पहिले दक्षिणतिर रहेको र चोकबाट मात्र प्रवेश गर्न मिल्ने गुम्बाको रेखदेख गर्ने व्यक्ति बताउँछन् (L09) ।  सन् १९७० को अन्तिमतिर लो मान्थाङबाट आएका एक लामाले चोकमा दुई तल्ले भवन बनाएका थिए । यसको भुँइतल्लामा अस्तबल राखिएको थियो भने माथिल्लो तल्लामा उनी आफै बस्थे (U10 जसलाई अहिले VIP room भनिन्छ) । गुम्बाको पूर्वी मोहडामा रहेको छाना सहितको प्रवेशमार्ग कहिले बनाइयो भन्ने जानकारीमा छैन । यहाँको रेखदेख गर्ने व्यक्तिका अनुसार तिनै लामाले गुम्बाको कुनाकुनामा रहेका छोर्तेनहरूको पुनर्निर्माण गरेका थिए ।सन् २००३-२००४ मा जोन सण्डे नामका व्यक्तिको निर्देशनमा गुम्बाको उत्तरी भागको पुनर्निर्माण गरिएको थियो । यसका लागि अमेरिकन हिमालयन फाउन्डेशनले आर्थिक सहयोग गरेको थियो ।

historical_events.event_description: The temple was restored between 2003-2005 by The American Himalayan Foundation under the leadership of John Sanday (Sanday Associates, Kathmandu).No project document could be located.The work included the rebuilding of the main temple's roof and the cleaning and consolidation of the murals in the sanctum.

Lo Gekhar's foundation is recorded in the Pema Katang (pad+ma bka’ thang ), a text containing the biography of Padmasambhava, the teacher credited with taming of local deities across the Himalayas. This text was discovered by the treasure revealer Orgyen Lingpa (o rgyan gling pa; b. 1323), his date thus providing a terminus ante quem for the original temple. The relevant account is found in canto 62, recording the completion of Samyé Monastery, and is translated as follows (with explanatory additions in square brackets):“At Lobo [= Mustang], the place which is as if a rakṣasī [a demoness] were lying on her back,place on her heart a monastery with nine floors,a stupa on her navel,another small and black one on her head,and one hundred and eight on her four limbs!In Malgro is the naga king called Shines in Malgro [= mal gro gzi can ].He has great influence in Tibet;I will establish for him a naga treasure; I want his life philtre [= srog chu - life water]."And the Guru came along into Malgro.Keeping his promise, shaking the depths, giving solid explanations,and having given treasure and a place of worship for the nagas, he received the life philtre.However, no oath bound the mind of the nagas, so to keep them silent,he erected at Lobo the monastery of White Virtue [= dge dkar, Gekar].”Accordingly, Lo Gekhar is this monastery of White Virtue, and the surrounding chörten and springs are part of the holy site. This account also explains why Lo Gekhar is of great cultural and religious importance to the Mustang region and to Tibetan Buddhism at large. The temple is frequently visited by pilgrims from the region and beyond.
In 1956 Snellgrove visited Upper Mustang and recorded a detailed description of Lo Gekar in his bookHimalayan Pilgrimage.
